newsitem.title: UK: UK shoppers defer payment, ignore card costs-poll.
newsitem.headline: UK shoppers defer payment, ignore card costs-poll.

text.p: Most British people will let their credit cards take the strain of Christmas shopping this year but few consider the cost of the card and many will still be paying their festive bills in June 1997, research from a US bank shows.
Connecticut-based People's Bank, newly established in the UK in Northampton, is aiming to carve out a slice of the UK market.

Its poll of 1,026 adults in Britain conducted at the end of November showed half those questioned expected to spend the same as last year but 37 percent would spend more. Over half expected to spend up to 400 stg, and another quarter up to 1,000 stg. Of those using credit cards, 11 percent will still be paying off the card next June, although most (61 percent) hoped to clear it by February. Only 25 percent had shopped around for a cheap credit card.

Londoners are more likely to use credit cards at Christmas (56 percent compared with 38 percent nationally) and people aged 35-44 prefer to use plastic payment (53 percent compared to 38 percent nationally).
